es: Escribir un párrafo persuasivo con una afirmación enfática (so/such), una pregunta retórica, un tricolon y una llamada a la acción.

teaching.en: Our city has such heavy traffic that a short commute takes an hour.
teaching.es: Nuestra ciudad tiene un tráfico tan pesado que un trayecto corto dura una hora.
teaching.explanationEs: Such + adjetivo + nombre incontable (heavy traffic) + that.
segments: Our city has such heavy traffic that
a short commute takes an hour.
teaching.audioText: Our city has such heavy traffic that a short commute takes an hour.

teaching.en: A bicycle is so cheap that almost everyone can use one.
teaching.es: Una bicicleta es tan barata que casi todo el mundo puede usar una.
teaching.explanationEs: So + adjetivo solo + that: tan… que.
segments: A bicycle is so cheap that
teaching.audioText: A bicycle is so cheap that almost everyone can use one.

teaching.en: Why should our community breathe pollution every day?
teaching.es: ¿Por qué debería nuestra comunidad respirar contaminación todos los días?
teaching.explanationEs: Pregunta retórica: Why should…? No espera respuesta.
teaching.audioText: Why should our community breathe pollution every day?

teaching.en: Bikes are cheap, quick and clean, so the benefit is obvious.
teaching.es: Las bicis son baratas, rápidas y limpias, así que la ventaja es obvia.
teaching.explanationEs: Tricolon: tres adjetivos con la misma forma cierran el argumento.
segments: Bikes are cheap, quick and clean,
teaching.audioText: Bikes are cheap, quick and clean, so the benefit is obvious.

teaching.en: We must convince the council to build a bicycle station near the school.
teaching.es: Debemos convencer al consejo de construir una estación de bicicletas cerca del colegio.
teaching.explanationEs: Convince someone to + verbo; la frase sirve de llamada a la acción.
segments: We must convince the council to build
a bicycle station near the school.
teaching.audioText: We must convince the council to build a bicycle station near the school.

teaching.en: There is so much pollution that the community cannot breathe.
teaching.es: Hay tanta contaminación que la comunidad no puede respirar.
teaching.explanationEs: So much + nombre incontable; so many + nombre plural.
teaching.audioText: There is so much pollution that the community cannot breathe.

prompt.es: Elige la versión enfática: «Es un tráfico tan pesado que nadie llega a tiempo.»

feedback.es: Traffic es incontable y va tras el adjetivo: such + adjetivo + nombre, sin a; so no admite nombre.

hint.es: Traffic es un nombre incontable: no lleva a.

feedback.es: Tras el hueco solo hay un adjetivo, así que se usa so.

hint.es: Empieza por la palabra interrogativa: Why should…

prompt.es: Elige el tricolon paralelo para hablar de las bicis.

Bikes are safe, simple and fun.
Bikes are safe, they are simple and to have fun.

prompt.es: Dale énfasis con such: «Es una idea muy buena.»

It is such a great idea.

feedback.es: Con a + adjetivo + nombre singular contable se usa such a: such a good idea.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada estructura con lo que exige después.

feedback.es: So acompaña a un adjetivo; such necesita un nombre, con a si es contable singular y sin a si es incontable.

prompt.es: Escucha el párrafo y elige qué propone la oradora.

choices.text: A new bus line across the city.
A ban on all cars in the centre.
A plan for public bicycles to reduce delays.

feedback.es: Propone bicicletas públicas como solución a los retrasos; no habla de autobuses ni de prohibir coches.

origin.audio: Our streets are so crowded that a ten-minute trip takes forty minutes. Why should we accept such a waste of time? Public bicycles are cheap, quick and clean. Let us ask the council to begin the plan.

prompt.es: Completa las tres frases del párrafo.

feedback.es: So much + incontable, such a + adjetivo + nombre y so + adjetivo solo.

prompt.es: Escribe un párrafo persuasivo sobre bicicletas públicas (75-170 palabras).

answer.text: Our neighbourhood has such heavy traffic that a short trip to school takes forty minutes. Who wants to breathe pollution every morning? Public bicycles are cheap, quick and clean, and they are so simple that anyone can use one. They would help students, workers and families, and they would make our streets calmer, safer and greener. Why should we wait another year for a better community? Let us ask the council to build a bicycle station near every school. Sign the petition today, and together we can change how our neighbourhood moves.
accepted: Our neighbourhood has such heavy traffic that a short trip to school takes forty minutes. Who wants to breathe pollution every morning? Public bicycles are cheap, quick and clean, and they are so simple that anyone can use one. They would help students, workers and families, and they would make our streets calmer, safer and greener. Why should we wait another year for a better community? Let us ask the council to build a bicycle station near every school. Sign the petition today, and together we can change how our neighbourhood moves.

Our city has such a serious traffic problem that parents are afraid to walk to school. Why should our children breathe pollution every day? A public bicycle is cheap, quick and clean, and it is so easy to use that everybody can try it. Bicycles would bring us a real benefit: less noise, less pollution and more time. We must convince the council to build a bicycle station near the school. Please join our campaign and sign the petition this week, because our community needs a better street.

feedback.es: Un párrafo persuasivo completo abre con énfasis, pregunta, enumera tres ventajas y termina con una petición concreta.

origin.text: Convence a tu comunidad de instalar bicicletas públicas. Incluye una afirmación con such o so, una pregunta retórica, un tricolon y una llamada a la acción dirigida al consejo.

prompt.es: Elige la frase con el énfasis correcto.

choices.text: It was such a loud speech that everyone listened.
It was so a loud speech that everyone listened.
It was such loud that everyone listened.

feedback.es: Con a + adjetivo + nombre se usa such: such a loud speech; so no admite nombre y such necesita uno.

prompt.es: Completa: «Hay tantos coches que la calle parece un aparcamiento.»

feedback.es: So many + nombre plural contable + that expresa cantidad con énfasis.

origin.text: There are ___ many cars that the street looks like a car park.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Pidamos al consejo que empiece ahora.»

answer.text: Let us ask the council to start now

feedback.es: La llamada a la acción usa Let us + verbo: aquí, ask the council to + verbo.
